message.content:
Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray and CT scan demonstrate bilateral pulmonary nodules and prominent bilateral hilar/mediastinal lymphadenopathy, which are classic radiographic features of sarcoidosis (often described as the "sarcoid galaxy sign" on CT when smaller nodules cluster around larger ones). This pattern distinguishes it from unilateral TB, heart failure effusions, or metastatic disease without adenopathy.
